is_acceptable_family_b_analogue: NO; it is acceptable as a native vLLM chunked-prefill test but not as an isolated simulator Family-B reproduction.

rows.consequence: Real FULL has a much larger per-iteration budget than Family-B full; 3200-token hogs fit in one iteration and can leave room for decode/short-prefill work.
rows.simulator_implementation: full_prefill uses GreedyArrivalPrefillControlPolicy plus max_prefill_chunk_tokens=65536, decode_first=False under enable_decode_prefill_contention=True; an earlier hog can consume the whole 512-token step budget.
rows.vllm_0_27_1_analogue: --no-enable-chunked-prefill with max_num_batched_tokens=4096; waiting request is admitted only if its full prompt fits remaining token budget.

rows.consequence: The real chunk size is about 8x the simulator small chunk and is coupled to total batch budget.
rows.vllm_0_27_1_analogue: --enable-chunked-prefill and max_num_batched_tokens=512; actual chunks are determined by remaining token budget, often 510-512 tokens in the diagnostic trace.

rows.consequence: Modern vLLM does not match the old v0.4.2-style shared FCFS simulator abstraction exactly.
rows.simulator_implementation: Family-B v2 does not rely on decode_first; decode_priority_chunked was dropped because it is a twin on clean traces.
rows.vllm_0_27_1_analogue: vLLM V1 scheduler has no separate decode phase; it schedules running requests first, then waiting requests, against one token budget.

rows.consequence: Treatment changes chunking and total scheduled-token budget together; this is a bundled scheduling/budget intervention.
rows.simulator_implementation: step_token_budget=512 shared across prefill and decode in Family-B v2.
rows.vllm_0_27_1_analogue: FULL required max_num_batched_tokens=4096; CHUNKED used 512. Disabled chunked prefill with 512 is rejected by vLLM when max_model_len=4096.

rows.consequence: Queueing exists, but late waiting requests are not interleaved with running prefill chunks the same way as simulator late-prefill crumbs.
rows.simulator_implementation: simulator GPU active sequence model with stepwise token budget and greedy arrival admission.
rows.vllm_0_27_1_analogue: max_num_seqs=4; scheduler first visits running requests, then promotes waiting requests while token and sequence slots remain.

rows.consequence: Observed overlap exists, but it is not the same natural-trace FCFS interaction that created Family-B v2 wins.
rows.simulator_implementation: decode requests consume one token in the same shared FCFS pass under decode_first=False, or first under decode-protected mode.
rows.vllm_0_27_1_analogue: running decode requests are scheduled before waiting requests; running decode and running prefill chunks can share an iteration.

rows.consequence: A long request once admitted under chunked mode can repeatedly consume budget while late requests remain waiting.
rows.simulator_implementation: policy admission is greedy arrival order; fixed variants differ only by service_model kwargs.
rows.vllm_0_27_1_analogue: FCFS waiting queue, but already-running requests are always considered before waiting admissions.

rows.consequence: Absolute service ratios are hardware/model dependent, not simulator-step commensurate.
rows.simulator_implementation: discrete 1 ms steps; token cost represented by counts against step budget.
rows.vllm_0_27_1_analogue: real kernels on RTX 5060 Ti; measured 3200-token single-request TTFT about 76.7 ms, representative decode ITL about 5.91 ms.

rows.consequence: Measurement is valid, but underlying service events differ.

rows.vllm_0_27_1_analogue: client-side streaming first-token timestamp from OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

rows.consequence: Useful for ratio diagnostics, not a direct simulator-step mapping.
rows.simulator_implementation: one decoded token per active decode request per step.
rows.vllm_0_27_1_analogue: streamed token inter-arrival approximated by (E2E - TTFT)/(output_tokens-1); batching and kernels are real.

rows.consequence: KV pressure was not active and should not be used for mechanism claims here.
